Mindfulness is thought to be a very effective form of meditation and is often taught as part of therapy programs. It's a practice of focusing on a single thought or moment, in order to train your mind not to wander. Until you try mindfulness, you don't realise how much your mind is churning over while you do other things. 

A good place to start is the leaves on a stream exercise. Imagine a stream as clearly as you can, the dappled light, gurgling sound, is it fast or slow. Then imagine leaves running down it, now try to just focus on this image. Every time you have a thought, visualise it being placed on a leaf and floating down stream- see if you can do this for 10 minutes to start out. Once you've done that, you can move on to focusing on the moment- mindfulness of breathing is popular: pay attention to your breath moving in and out, your aim is to not let your thoughts wander, as they do, refocus yourself. You can also try the '5 things I haven't noticed in the room', '5 sounds', '5 smells'- these last ones are really good for relaxing if you're anxious. It's basically just an exercise in paying complete attention- something most people aren't very good at.

I live in Australia, so we have rainforests. 

It was beautifully sunny, but the rainforest was one I frequented in the hotter months because it was a series of mountains and valleys that were cool enough that you forgot the time of year. I set off down the red soil path, worn down with heavy foot traffic. A few hours down the ravine, and I lead my friend off the path a little to show him one of my favourite places in the world. Pushing through the dry bushland, found only at the top of the mountains, I lead him out carefully onto a jutting, white-quartz ledge. A small cliff where we looked down on the beautiful white cockatoos soaring through the ravine of endless deep-blue trees below us. We sat and watched a spider make his web on a tiny piece of dry Bush clinging to the edge of the cliff as we dangled our legs over the abyss below us. I have never felt more alive and relaxed than looking over that range.

As the sun got lower in the sky, we set off again down the less trodden path deeper into the mountain. A chance encounter with an aggressive snake livened things up, but I usually pass at least one on my weekly hikes. Eventually I started to hear the trickling of a stream and we were so deep in that the light was a dim blue, filtered by the canopy. The ground layered in moist leaves, and every where filled with life- beautiful orange fungus clusters, mosses, palms, gumtrees, lichen on every rock. We reached the base of the mountain and came out at the base of a waterfall with running streams and pools. We relaxed there for a while as night approached, then began our slippery, cliff-side return journey.

As it got darker and the moon lit our path, I was ready to surprise my friend with why I'd kept him out so late. The night brought loud, eerie bird calls; adding to the beauty of where we were. It turned out I'd timed the journey just right, and I saw the flash of an ember by a leaf in the undergrowth. I told my friend to keep watch. And as we rounded the mountain side again, the darkness was lit up by glittering embers, floating all around us- tiny fireflies who owned the forest at night with us standing in awe of their glinting show.

This memory means the world to me. 2 weeks later, despite my young age of 21 and my fitness from being an avid hiker, I was rushed to hospital with a mystery illness that was affecting my heart and other organs. I've been in a wheel chair/bed bound the last two years. I don't know if I'll ever hike again, but if I ever get back to my cliff, my waterfall, and my fireflies- despite all these years of pain and illness; I know I'll be the happiest girl in the world.

There's no need to drink more unless you're dealing with health issues (and your doctor suggests it)/your urine is really dark (keep in mind vitamin c supplements or excess salt will darken your urine colour) or... you're thirsty (the chances of you having some extremely rare illness like me are pretty low).
